fields.description:
## Context

Complete bridge portability across local shells, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, and bare
environments without breaking checked-out workflows or environments that still use the legacy
reconcile vocabulary.

This story coordinates two independently releasable children:

1. A runner-neutral bridge entrypoint plus thin GitHub Actions, Jenkins, and GitLab wrappers.
2. Provider-neutral destructive-repair pause ownership for `fsck --repair` and `doctor --repair`.

The children are intentionally dependency-free. Their implementation ownership is otherwise
non-overlapping; their additive release-note updates were developed and landed sequentially. Each
child preserves old vocabulary, signatures, defaults, messages, exit behavior, and mutation
boundaries while adding the new noun-based bridge route. They may be reviewed and submitted
separately or shipped together after both gates are green.

GitHub-specific mirror health (`src/rebar/mirror_guard.py`) and optional GitHub step-summary
reporting are outside bridge execution. They remain unchanged and are not evidence for or against
the provider neutrality of the bridge runner.

## Plan

1. Review and claim each child independently.
2. Implement each child under RED-first held-out TDD.
3. Require `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, and no unresolved Gerrit comments before submission.
4. Verify legacy reconcile callers and checked-out workflows continue to operate.
5. Close this story after both children have landed and closed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The runner-neutral bridge child is closed with its Gerrit change merged.
- [x] The provider-neutral destructive-repair child is closed with its Gerrit change merged.
- [x] Checked-out workflows that still invoke `rebar reconcile --mode ...` retain their behavior.
- [x] Environments using legacy reconcile modes retain their published defaults and exit behavior.
- [x] Local, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, and bare bridge execution use the packaged Python core in `src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py` through exactly `rebar bridge run`; no repository-local runner script is required.
- [x] `src/rebar/_commands/_repair_pause.py` owns destructive-repair schedule safety through the provider-neutral durable gate lifecycle: it reads the existing pause snapshot, calls `set_pause`, and clears only its observed OID through `release(..., ref_lock.GATE_REF, ...)`.
- [x] `tests/scripts/graph/test_repair_pause_ownership.py` proves no GitHub CLI dependency: it rejects subprocess argv beginning with `gh`, runs destructive repair successfully, and asserts `gh_calls == []`.

## File impact

Owned by the two child tasks. This coordination story changes no files directly; its recorded
file-impact paths are child-owned completion evidence supplied to the bounded close-gate prefetch.
fields.title: Make the bridge portable across local, GitHub, Jenkins, GitLab, and bare environments
